start.summary: Starts a function on another thread and comes back at once with a handle to it.
params: the function to run, passed as a value
start.returns: the handle of the task, to be passed to the other functions of this module.
start.note: The task runs **outside** the tick of the game: to touch blocks, entities or anything else of the world from inside it, wrap that part in `dock`.

wait.summary: Waits for the task to finish and returns its value.
wait.note: It blocks the thread that calls it. Calling it from the tick of the game means stopping the server until the task ends; from there use `wait` of `core.mc.system`, which knows how to wait without blocking the tick.

next.summary: Waits for the task to finish without asking for its value.
examples: for(tasks, task.next(_));   // waits for all of them

done.summary: Whether the task has already finished, without waiting for it.

value.summary: The value of the task when it has one, without waiting.
value.returns: the value produced, or `null` when it is not ready.

count.summary: How many tasks are running right now.
params: optional: only the ones of that group
count.returns: `num` — the number of tasks in flight.
examples:
// waiting for everything to quiet down
while(task.count() > 0, 1000, task.sleep(50));

send.summary: Sends a value into a running task, where a `yield` is waiting for it.

has_next.summary: Whether the task has a value waiting to be read.

yield.summary: From inside a task: hands a value out and suspends until somebody asks for the next one.
params: what to hand out; without it, `null`
yield.note: It is what turns a task into a generator: it produces on demand instead of computing everything and holding it in memory.

dock.summary: Runs the expression on the main thread of the game and waits for its result.
params: what to run inside the tick
examples:
// inside a task: the world can only be touched from here
task.dock(block.set([0, 64, 0], 'stone'));
dock.note: Everything in `core.mc.*` needs this when it is called from a task. Keep what goes inside it short: it runs in the tick, and while it runs the server waits.

synchronize.summary: Runs the expression with a lock held, so two tasks never do it at the same time.
params: the name of the lock, any value; the same name means the same lock
examples:
// read and write are two steps: without the lock a count gets lost
task.synchronize('counter', counter = counter + 1);
synchronize.note: The lock is reentrant (a synchronised function can call another one on the same lock) and fair (whoever waits gets in in the order they arrived). Single operations (an assignment, a `put`, a `remove`) are already atomic on their own and need no lock; it is *sequences* that do.

sleep.summary: Suspends the current thread for a while.
sleep.note: Inside a task it is fine. On the main thread it stops the server: to wait in the game there is `schedule` in `core.mc.event`, which counts ticks and lets the world go on.
